The seventh Month, which that New Moon did introduce or begin, and in which, besides other Solemnities, they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, which the Hebrew Doctours call <ns0:hi>the Feast</ns0:hi> by way of eminency, and <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sephus</ns0:hi> affirms to have been the most sacred and the chief of all the Jewish Feasts.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 23. 24: Num. 10. 10.</ns0:note> this <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a statute for Israel, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> a law of the God of Jacob <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">For this is no humane device but an appointment and command of the great God and your Lord.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p>This <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To wit, the blowing of Trumpets:</ns0:note> he ordained in Joseph <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Among the po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sterity of <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> to wit, the people of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> as is evident both from the foregoing Verse where they are called <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and from the following words in this Verse, where they are described by their coming out of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> which was common to all the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> who are sometimes callsed by the name of <ns0:hi>Ioseph;</ns0:hi> of which see on Psal. 80. 1.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> a testimo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Either 1. For a Law, which is oft called a <ns0:hi>testimony.</ns0:hi> Or rather, 2. For a witness and memorial of that glorious deliverance mentioned in the following words. For 1. That this was a <ns0:hi>statute</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>law</ns0:hi> he had expressed, <ns0:hi>Vers.</ns0:hi> 4. which it is not likely that he would here repeat, especially<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in a more dark and doubtful phrase. 2. He seems to declare the end of that Law, which was to be a <ns0:hi>testimony.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, when he <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To wit, God, <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>ordained,</ns0:hi> as was now said.</ns0:note> went out <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">As a Captain in the head, or on the behalf of his people.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> against.</ns0:note> through the land of Egypt <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To execute his judgments upon that Land or People. Or, <ns0:hi>against, &c.</ns0:hi> to destroy it. Or, <ns0:hi>out of</ns0:hi> it, as both ancient and other Interpreters render this Particle <ns0:hi>al,</ns0:hi> which is elsewhere put for <ns0:hi>meal,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>meal</ns0:hi> is put for <ns0:hi>min, from</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>out of,</ns0:hi> as is manifest by comparing 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 21. 8. with 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 33. 8. So this Text notes the time when this and the other Feasts were instituted; which was at, or presently after their coming out of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> even at <ns0:hi>Sinai.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: where I <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) My progenitors, for all the successive Generations of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> make one body, and are sometimes spoken of as one person.</ns0:note> heard a language <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> I <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> not.</ns0:note> understood not <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either 1. The Language of God himself speaking from Heaven at <ns0:hi>Sinai,</ns0:hi> which was strange and terrible to me. Or rather, 2. The Egyptian Language, which at first was very ungrateful and unknown to the Israelites, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 42. 23. and probably continued so for some considerable time, because they were much separated both in place and conversation from the Egyptians through <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi>'s pious and prudent design. This Exposition is confirmed from <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 114. 1. where this very thing is mentioned as an aggravation of their misery, and from other places of Scripture where this is spoken of as a curse and plague to be with a people of strange Language, as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 28. 49. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 5, 15.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 I removed his shoulder from the burden <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I delivered him from burdensome slavery.</ns0:note>: his hands <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> passed away.</ns0:note> were delivered from the pots <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">As this word is taken 1 Sam. 2. 14. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 35. 13. Or <ns0:hi>baskets,</ns0:hi> as it sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 10. 7. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 24. 2. In the general it seems to note all those Vessels wherein they carried water, straw, lime, bricks, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:480" />7 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 2. 23.</ns0:note> Thou calledst in trouble <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">At the Red Sea, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 14. 10, 11, 12.</ns0:note>, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">From the dark and cloudy pillar, whence I thundred and fought against the <ns0:hi>Egyptians.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 13. 21. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 14. 19, 24. Others refer this to the thunder at <ns0:hi>Sinai.</ns0:hi> But at that time they were not <ns0:hi>in trouble,</ns0:hi> but in a safe and glorious condition.</ns0:note>: I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 17. 6, 7: Num. 20. 13.</ns0:note> proved thee at the waters of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> strife.</ns0:note> Meri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bah. Selah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 * Hear, O my people, and I will testifie un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to<ns0:note place="margin">Psal. 50. 7.</ns0:note> thee <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Concerning my will and thy duty. I will give thee Sta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tutes and Judgments, in the execution of which thou mayst live and be happy for ever. This God did presently after he brought them from <ns0:hi>Meribah,</ns0:hi> even at <ns0:hi>Sinai.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me;</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 There shall no strange God be in thee: nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther shalt thou worship any strange God <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Thou shalt renounce all false Gods and worships, and worship me onely.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the LORD thy God which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Either 1. To pray for mercies: Ask freely and abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dantly and boldly (as this Phrase oft signifies) whatsoever you need, or in reason can desire. Or 2. To receive the mercies which I am ready to give you.</ns0:note>, and I will fill it <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">I will give or grant them all, upon condition of your obedience.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 But my people would not hearken to my voice: and Israel would none of me <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>did not assent to me,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>acquiesce in me,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>obey me,</ns0:hi> or my commands.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 7. 42. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 14. 16.</ns0:note> So I gave them up <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> to the hardness of their hearts or imagi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nations.</ns0:note> unto their own hearts lust <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Upon their obstinate and oft-repeated Rebellions and Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jections of my Grace and Mercy offered to them I withdrew all the restraints of my providence and my Holy Spirit and Grace from them, and wholly left them to follow their own vain and foolish imaginations and wicked lusts.</ns0:note>: <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> they walked in their own counsels <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">They practised those things both in common conversation and in re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ligious Worship which were most agreeable not to my com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mands or counsels, but to their own fancies and inclinations, as appeared in the Golden Calf and many other things.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 32. 29. Isa. 48. 18.</ns0:note> O that my people had hearkened unto me, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> Israel had walked in my ways!</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 I would soon have subdued their Enemies <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Those Remainders of the <ns0:hi>Canaanites</ns0:hi> whom now for their unbelief and apostacy I have left in the Land to be snares and plagues to them.</ns0:note>, and turned my hand against their adversaries.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 The haters of the LORD <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">All the haters and enemies of God's people, as the neighbouring Nations were, whom he calls <ns0:hi>haters of God,</ns0:hi> partly because they hated the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> for God's sake, and for the singularity of their Religious Worship, as the Heathen oft declared: and partly to shew the strict League and Union which was betwixt God and them, by virtue whereof God had declared all their Friends and Enemies to be his own, which was a great aggravation of their wickedness.</ns0:note> should <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> yielded seigned obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> lied.</ns0:note> have submitted themselves unto him <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Should have professed and owned their subjection to them. For the Phrase see on <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 18. 44.</ns0:note>: but their time <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e. Israel's</ns0:hi> time; the Relative belonging to the remoter Antecedent; as it is in many other places of Scripture, whereof I have formerly given Instances. By <ns0:hi>their time</ns0:hi> he means either 1. Their happy time, as <ns0:hi>life</ns0:hi> is oft put for an happy life or state, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 34. 12. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 49. 18. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 4. 1. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 5. 33, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Or 2. The duration of their Common-wealth.</ns0:note> should have endured for e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Lasted for a very long time; whereas now their latter and dolesul end is hastening towards them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 He should have fed them also <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> with the fat of wheat.</ns0:note> with the finest of the wheat: and with honey <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Either 1. Metaphorically, with all pleasant and precious fruits and with all delights, as all necessaries may be ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressed under the name of <ns0:hi>wheat.</ns0:hi> Or rather 2. Properly: this Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> being commended for its excellent and plentiful honey; and the Bees there did oft-times harbour and make their honey in the holes of Rocks and such like places, from which it flowed down upon the ground. See <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32. 13. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 14. 25, 26.</ns0:note> out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.</ns0:p>
